rationale: In the seminal cohort establishing autosomal dominant intellectual developmental disorder-77 (OMIM #621415), Willim et al. (2024) identified 33 individuals with pathogenic heterozygous LRRC7 variants. Hyperphagia-associated obesity was reported as a notable but non-universal feature present in a distinct subset rather than the entire cohort (including 4 of 14 individuals harboring truncating loss-of-function variants, and 5 of 33 individuals overall, 15.2%). Subsequent single-case reports (e.g., Khan et al., 2026) corroborate that hyperphagia and class-II obesity can manifest with LRRC7 variants (including missense variants), confirming it represents an important behavioral/metabolic sub-phenotype rather than an obligate or universal syndromic finding.

evidence.text: Willim et al. delineate 33 individuals with dominant LRRC7 variants presenting with neurodevelopmental abnormalities; hyperphagia-associated obesity was noted as a distinct recurrent phenotype emerging later in childhood and was observed in 4 of 14 individuals with truncating variants, and in 5 of 33 individuals overall.

evidence.text: Khan et al. identified a novel de novo missense variant in LRRC7 [c.2660C>T; p.(Pro887Leu)] in a proband with intellectual disability, hypotonia, global developmental delay, hyperphagia, and class-II obesity, demonstrating that hyperphagia and obesity recur outside the original cohort and are not restricted exclusively to loss-of-function/truncating alleles.

conflicts: Age-dependent onset of hyperphagia and obesity (starting in mid-childhood or adolescence) implies that younger pediatric individuals in cross-sectional cohorts might not yet have manifested the trait, which could artificially deflate the reported cross-sectional frequency below its lifetime penetrance.

new_directions.question_text: What is the longitudinal penetrance of hyperphagia and obesity in LRRC7 post-pubertal individuals compared to pre-pubertal individuals?
new_directions.rationale: Because abnormal eating behaviors and hyperphagia in synaptopathies frequently emerge during later childhood, longitudinal follow-up is necessary to establish true lifetime penetrance across variant types.

new_directions.question_text: Does LRRC7 disruption directly dysregulate hypothalamic leptin-melanocortin circuitry, or is hyperphagia secondary to behavioral impulse control/autism spectrum pathology?
new_directions.rationale: Densin-180 functions at postsynaptic densities; establishing whether hyperphagia is driven by homeostatic hypothalamic appetite centers or hedonic/executive control circuits will clarify therapeutic targets such as MC4R agonists.
